verses.text: Then Joseph could no longer control himself before all his attendants, and he cried out, "Send everyone away from me!" So none of them were with Joseph when he made himself known to his brothers.
But he wept so loudly that the Egyptians heard him, and Pharaoh's household soon heard of it.
Joseph said to his brothers, "I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?" But they were unable to answer him, because they were terrified in his presence.
Then Joseph said to his brothers, "Please come near me." And they did so. "I am Joseph, your brother," he said, "the one you sold into Egypt!
And now, do not be distressed or angry with yourselves that you sold me into this place, because it was to save lives that God sent me before you.
For the famine has covered the land these two years, and there will be five more years without plowing or harvesting.
God sent me before you to preserve you as a remnant on the earth and to save your lives by a great deliverance.
Therefore it was not you who sent me here, but God, who has made me a father to Pharaoh—lord of all his household and ruler over all the land of Egypt.
Now return quickly to my father and tell him, 'This is what your son Joseph says: God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me without delay.
You shall settle in the land of Goshen and be near me—you and your children and grandchildren, your flocks and herds, and everything you own.
And there I will provide for you, because there will be five more years of famine. Otherwise, you and your household and everything you own will come to destitution.'
Behold! You and my brother Benjamin can see that I, Joseph, am the one speaking with you.
Tell my father about all my splendor in Egypt and everything you have seen. And bring my father down here quickly."
Then Joseph threw his arms around his brother Benjamin and wept, and Benjamin wept as they embraced.
Joseph kissed each of his brothers as he wept over them. And afterward his brothers talked with him.
When the news reached Pharaoh's house that Joseph's brothers had come, Pharaoh and his servants were pleased.
Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Tell your brothers, 'Do as follows: Load your animals and return to the land of Canaan.
Then bring your father and your families and return to me. I will give you the best of the land of Egypt, and you shall eat from the fat of the land.'
You are also directed to tell them: 'Take wagons from the land of Egypt for your young children and your wives, and bring your father and come back.
But pay no regard to your belongings, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.'"
So the sons of Israel did as they were told. Joseph gave them wagons as Pharaoh had instructed, and he also gave them provisions for their journey.
He gave new garments to each of them, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred shekels of silver and five sets of clothes.
And he sent to his father the following: ten donkeys loaded with the best of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain and bread and provisions for his father's journey.
Then Joseph sent his brothers on their way, and as they were leaving, he said to them, "Do not quarrel on the way!"
So the brothers went up out of Egypt and came to their father Jacob in the land of Canaan.
"Joseph is still alive," they said, "and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt!" But Jacob was stunned, for he did not believe them.
However, when they relayed all that Joseph had told them, and when he saw the wagons that Joseph had sent to carry him back, the spirit of their father Jacob was revived.
"Enough!" declared Israel. "My son Joseph is still alive! I will go to see him before I die."

context.author: Genesis names no author. Jewish and Christian tradition, and the New Testament’s way of speaking of “the Law of Moses” (Luke 24:44), credit the five books of the Law to Moses. Many scholars think Genesis was gathered and shaped from older sources over a long time, and a few remarks look back from a later day: “at that time the Canaanites were in the land” (Genesis 12:6).
context.genre: Family narrative: the story of Joseph and his brothers (Genesis 37 to 50)
context.audience: Israel, the twelve tribes, learning how their fathers came down to Egypt and how God turned evil to good
context.setting: Joseph can no longer control himself. He sends out his attendants and weeps so loudly that the Egyptians hear (vv.1-2). “I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?” (v.3). His brothers are terrified. “Please come near me,” he says. “I am Joseph, your brother… the one you sold into Egypt!” (v.4). “Do not be distressed or angry with yourselves that you sold me into this place, because it was to save lives that God sent me before you” (v.5). Five more years of famine are coming; “God sent me before you to preserve you as a remnant on the earth… Therefore it was not you who sent me here, but God” (vv.6-8). He tells them to bring their father quickly and settle in the land of Goshen near him (vv.9-13). He embraces Benjamin and kisses all his brothers, weeping, “and afterward his brothers talked with him” (vv.14-15), the brothers who once “could not speak a kind word to him” (37:4). Pharaoh offers “the best of the land of Egypt” and wagons for the journey (vv.16-20). Joseph sends them off with gifts, adding, “Do not quarrel on the way!” (vv.21-24). Jacob is stunned and does not believe them, but when he sees the wagons, “the spirit of their father Jacob was revived. ‘Enough!’ declared Israel. ‘My son Joseph is still alive! I will go to see him before I die’” (vv.26-28).
context.custom: Goshen lay in the eastern Nile delta, good grazing land on the route from Canaan, suited to a family of shepherds (46:34). Wagons (two-wheeled ox carts) were rare in the hill country of Canaan, so Pharaoh’s wagons were proof Jacob could see. “A father to Pharaoh” (v.8) is a title like the Egyptian father of the god, held by some high officials as trusted advisers of the king.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 46: Jacob sets out for Egypt, and God speaks to him at Beersheba.
context.timelineBible: Joseph sees God’s hand behind his brothers’ crime without excusing it: “it was not you who sent me here, but God” (v.8), words he repeats in 50:20. Stephen tells the council that “on their second visit, Joseph revealed his identity to his brothers” (Acts 7:13). Paul expresses the same faith: “God works all things together for the good of those who love Him” (Romans 8:28).

translation.meaning: Preservation of life, means of living. Joseph sees that God sent him ahead to keep the family alive.
What is left, a remnant. A key word of the prophets: God always keeps a remnant through judgment (Isaiah 10:20-22).
To live, to come back to life. Jacob’s spirit revives when he sees the wagons, and he says, “My son Joseph is still alive!” using the same verb.

gospelParallels.note: Joseph made himself known and called his father and family.
God works all things together for good.
The risen Jesus: it is I Myself; touch Me and see.

otBackground.note: You intended evil, but God intended it for good.
He sent a man before them.

overview.summary: Joseph reveals himself to his brothers, forgives them, tells them God sent him ahead to save lives, and sends them back with Pharaoh’s wagons to bring Jacob to Egypt.
overview.settingLine: Joseph’s house in Egypt, and Jacob’s tents in Canaan.
overview.placeName: The land of Goshen, in the eastern Nile delta (approximate)

history.t: Grazing land in the eastern delta, on the road from Canaan.
Egyptian carts proved the story to Jacob.

customs.t: Joseph weeps openly before his brothers; before, he hid his tears.
Changes of clothes were gifts of honor.

archaeology.t: Excavations at Tell el-Dab’a found a large population from Canaan in the Middle Bronze Age.
Two-wheeled carts appear in Egyptian tomb scenes.

overview.discussion: Joseph said, “it was not you who sent me here, but God” (v.8), without pretending the wrong never happened (v.4). What would it take for me to see God’s purpose in what someone did to me, and still forgive them?
overview.book: The book of Genesis · 50 chapters. Beginnings: creation, the fall, the flood and the nations, then God’s promise to Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
overview.author: Moses, by tradition

biblePlaces.name: The land of Goshen, in the eastern Nile delta (approximate)
